parameters.content:
## A · Loan product discovery (S1 crawl-time compile + S6 confidence guard)
Daily at 06:00, or run manually. For each source in `crawl_sources`, one at a time: check robots.txt → fetch pages → clean to structured text → SHA-256 → **unchanged? skip the LLM**. Otherwise extract through the LLM gateway → validate and compile rules in code → upsert with a criteria diff → close the crawl run.
`crawl_mode=fixtures` (default) reads saved pages from the `fixtures` container. `live` fetches the real sites with our User-Agent and a pause between requests.
Every failure path closes that source's run as `error`, so one bad source never stops the others.
Last, **Warm match cache** judges every cohort the active products can produce, so Workflow B finds them cached and makes no LLM call at match time.
**A second run skips the LLM by design** (pages unchanged, cohorts cached). `make demo-reset` forgets one page's hash and the warm cache, so the next run takes every branch.

### Failure paths
robots.txt disallowed or unreachable · a page not 200 · the LLM failed or the budget is spent · validation threw · upsert failed. Each one becomes an item with `run_status` and `error`, and goes to **Finish crawl run**, which records it in `crawl_runs`. Then the loop moves on to the next source.

-- First node of every workflow: all app_config switches as one JSON object (DECISIONS.md AD4).
-- Later nodes read a value as $('Load app_config').first().json.config.email_mode, and so on.
-- (No n8n expression braces in SQL files: the Postgres node evaluates them even inside comments.)
SELECT jsonb_object_agg(key, value) AS config
FROM app_config;

-- Workflow A: the enabled sources, one item each, in a stable order. robots_url is derived
-- here so workflow expressions never have to parse URLs.
SELECT source_id,
       slug,
       display_name,
       kind,
       page_urls,
       fixture_files,
       last_content_hash,
       regexp_replace(page_urls[1], '^(https?://[^/]+).*$', '\1') || '/robots.txt' AS robots_url
FROM crawl_sources
WHERE enabled
ORDER BY source_id;

-- Workflow A, after every source: products not seen for #1 days have left their page, so they
-- stop being matched. Returns a single count row so the node always emits one item.
WITH stale AS (
    UPDATE loan_products
    SET is_active = false
    WHERE is_active
      AND last_seen_at < now() - make_interval(days => $1::integer)
    RETURNING product_id
)
SELECT count(*) AS products_deactivated FROM stale;

-- Workflow A's final output: what this execution did, per source, plus totals.
-- Parameter: #1 execution id.
SELECT s.slug,
       r.status,
       r.http_status,
       r.products_found,
       r.llm_calls,
       r.tokens_in,
       r.tokens_out,
       r.error,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM loan_products p WHERE p.source_id = s.source_id AND p.is_active)
           AS active_products
FROM crawl_runs r
JOIN crawl_sources s USING (source_id)
WHERE r.execution_id = $1
ORDER BY s.source_id;

-- Workflow A: open a crawl run for one source. It stays 'running' until finish_run.sql closes
-- it, so a run that dies midway is visible. Parameters: #1 execution id, #2 source id, #3 mode.
INSERT INTO crawl_runs (execution_id, source_id, mode)
VALUES ($1, $2::integer, $3)
RETURNING run_id, source_id, mode;

-- Workflow A: upsert one source's validated products in a single statement, and record a
-- criteria diff for every product that is new or whose criteria changed.
--
-- Parameters:
--   #1  products: JSON array produced by n8n/code/validate_products.js
--   #2  source_id
--   #3  crawl run id (links the history rows to the run that saw the change)
--   #4  content hash of the cleaned page text
--
-- Every CTE sees the same snapshot, so `previous` holds the criteria from before this upsert.
-- A product whose criteria change gets needs_review = true until someone clears it. A first
-- sighting writes a history row with old_criteria NULL, so every product has a starting point
-- for later diffs.
--
-- Products are matched on their identity within the source (lender + name, normalised:
-- migration 010), not the exact wording, so a re-extraction that names a product differently
-- updates it (and takes the new name) instead of adding a copy. Two entries of one extraction
-- with the same identity are one product: the one with more hard-filter fields is kept, as
-- validate_products.js does for exact repeats.
WITH extracted AS (
    SELECT p.*, product_identity(p.lender, p.product_name) AS identity_key, e.ord
    FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) WITH ORDINALITY AS e (item, ord)
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_to_record(e.item) AS p (
        lender              text,
        product_name        text,
        source_url          text,
        interest_rate_min   numeric,
        interest_rate_max   numeric,
        min_monthly_income  numeric,
        min_credit_score    smallint,
        min_age             smallint,
        max_age             smallint,
        allowed_employment  text[],
        soft_criteria       jsonb,
        field_confidence    jsonb,
        criteria_json       jsonb,
        criteria_hash       text
    )
),
incoming AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (identity_key) e.*
    FROM extracted e
    ORDER BY identity_key,
             num_nonnulls(min_age, max_age, min_credit_score, min_monthly_income,
                          allowed_employment, interest_rate_min) DESC,
             ord
),
previous AS (
    SELECT lp.identity_key, lp.criteria_json, lp.criteria_hash
    FROM loan_products lp
    JOIN incoming i ON lp.source_id = $2::integer AND lp.identity_key = i.identity_key
),
upserted AS (
    INSERT INTO loan_products AS lp (
        source_id, source_url, lender, product_name,
        interest_rate_min, interest_rate_max, min_monthly_income, min_credit_score,
        min_age, max_age, allowed_employment, soft_criteria, field_confidence,
        criteria_json, criteria_hash, content_hash, is_active, last_seen_at
    )
    SELECT $2::integer, source_url, lender, product_name,
           interest_rate_min, interest_rate_max, min_monthly_income, min_credit_score,
           min_age, max_age, allowed_employment, soft_criteria, field_confidence,
           criteria_json, criteria_hash, $4, true, now()
    FROM incoming
    ON CONFLICT (source_id, identity_key) DO UPDATE SET
        source_url         = EXCLUDED.source_url,
        lender             = EXCLUDED.lender,
        product_name       = EXCLUDED.product_name,
        interest_rate_min  = EXCLUDED.interest_rate_min,
        interest_rate_max  = EXCLUDED.interest_rate_max,
        min_monthly_income = EXCLUDED.min_monthly_income,
        min_credit_score   = EXCLUDED.min_credit_score,
        min_age            = EXCLUDED.min_age,
        max_age            = EXCLUDED.max_age,
        allowed_employment = EXCLUDED.allowed_employment,
        soft_criteria      = EXCLUDED.soft_criteria,
        field_confidence   = EXCLUDED.field_confidence,
        criteria_json      = EXCLUDED.criteria_json,
        needs_review       = lp.needs_review OR lp.criteria_hash <> EXCLUDED.criteria_hash,
        criteria_hash      = EXCLUDED.criteria_hash,
        content_hash       = EXCLUDED.content_hash,
        is_active          = true,
        last_seen_at       = now()
    RETURNING lp.product_id, lp.identity_key, lp.criteria_json,
              lp.criteria_hash, (lp.xmax = 0) AS inserted
),
-- Products of this source that the new extraction did not return are retired at once. Their
-- criteria predate the page as it reads now, and keeping them active kept stale, often looser,
-- rules matching customers until the stale-days sweep (docs/DECISIONS.md AD37). An empty
-- extraction retires nothing, so a failed read can't empty a source.
retired AS (
    UPDATE loan_products lp
    SET is_active = false
    WHERE lp.source_id = $2::integer
      AND lp.is_active
      AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM incoming)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM incoming i WHERE i.identity_key = lp.identity_key)
    RETURNING lp.product_id
),
history AS (
    INSERT INTO product_criteria_history (product_id, crawl_run_id, old_criteria, new_criteria, changed_fields)
    SELECT u.product_id,
           $3::bigint,
           p.criteria_json,
           u.criteria_json,
           ARRAY(
               SELECT k
               FROM (
                   SELECT jsonb_object_keys(u.criteria_json) AS k
                   UNION
                   SELECT jsonb_object_keys(COALESCE(p.criteria_json, '{}'::jsonb))
               ) AS keys
               WHERE (u.criteria_json -> k) IS DISTINCT FROM (p.criteria_json -> k)
               ORDER BY k
           )
    FROM upserted u
    LEFT JOIN previous p USING (identity_key)
    WHERE p.criteria_hash IS DISTINCT FROM u.criteria_hash
    RETURNING product_id, old_criteria IS NULL AS first_sighting
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM upserted)                                   AS products_upserted,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM upserted WHERE inserted)                    AS products_new,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM history WHERE NOT first_sighting)           AS products_changed,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM retired)                                    AS products_retired;

-- Workflow A: close a crawl run and update the source's bookkeeping in one statement.
--
-- Parameters: #1 run_id, #2 status, #3 http_status, #4 content_hash, #5 products_found,
--             #6 llm_calls, #7 tokens_in, #8 tokens_out, #9 error
--
-- On success ('changed' or 'unchanged') the source remembers the content hash, so the next run
-- can skip the LLM when the page hasn't changed. On 'unchanged' the source's products are
-- also marked as seen: they are still on the page, and without this they would be deactivated
-- after PRODUCT_STALE_DAYS of an unchanged page. Always returns exactly one row, so the
-- workflow's loop never stalls on an empty result.
WITH run AS (
    UPDATE crawl_runs
    SET status         = $2,
        http_status    = $3::integer,
        content_hash   = $4,
        products_found = $5::integer,
        llm_calls      = COALESCE($6::integer, 0),
        tokens_in      = COALESCE($7::integer, 0),
        tokens_out     = COALESCE($8::integer, 0),
        error          = $9,
        finished_at    = now()
    WHERE run_id = $1::bigint
    RETURNING run_id, source_id, status, content_hash
),
source AS (
    UPDATE crawl_sources s
    SET last_content_hash = run.content_hash,
        last_crawled_at   = now()
    FROM run
    WHERE s.source_id = run.source_id
      AND run.status IN ('changed', 'unchanged')
    RETURNING s.source_id
),
seen AS (
    UPDATE loan_products p
    SET last_seen_at = now()
    FROM run
    WHERE p.source_id = run.source_id
      AND p.is_active
      AND run.status = 'unchanged'
    RETURNING p.product_id
)
SELECT run.run_id,
       run.status,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM seen) AS products_touched
FROM run;
